title: Our Collaborators
text:
About This Project
    

The Yale School of Public Health Society Connectedness & Health Lab’s (SOCAH Lab) premier Church Closure Dashboard is designed to dynamically display metrics describing church closures down to the block group level over user-provided date ranges. Users can select regions to explore socioeconomic information alongside church closure metrics, or apply institutional filters to refine their view.
Shelby Golden, M.S. from the Yale School of Public Health Data Science and Data Equity team was contracted to review and update the data cleaning, validation, and harmonization methods previously employed by Insang Song, Ph.D. to generate data compatible with dynamic visualization on the dashboard map.
This codebase includes a GitHub Pages website outlining the development process and describing the pipeline for researchers interested in replicating results or preparing the raw data for their own work. Scripts include detailed annotations explaining the code and provide guidelines to help subsequent analysts reproduce results or adapt the process for improvements or other applications.
Project Principal Investigator (PI): Yusuf Ransome, M.P.H., Dr.P.H.
Project Manager: Katelyn Kostakis, M.P.H.
Developer and Analyst: Shelby Golden, M.S.

Our Collaborators
The Church Closure Dashboard is a collaborative effort led by the Yale School of Public Health Society Connectedness & Health Lab’s (SOCAH Lab).



















Yale Center for Research Computing





Access Restrictions and Requirements
Under the Data Use Agreements (DUAs) with Data Axle and the USPS API license, raw data cannot be publicly distributed and is stored locally in ~/KEEP LOCAL directories. Some code or results may also be restricted. All publicly distributed results are summarized, and publicly distributed code has been constructed to avoid referencing individual-level data. Executing the code below requires access to the raw data and results.
API keys are user-specific and, where applicable, instructions have been provided to help users obtain their own and configure them locally or on a High Performance Computer (HPC).


Data Disclaimer
This dashboard is intended for research and informational purposes. These data are provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind, explicit or implied, including but not limited to the warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and noninfringement. While every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy and completeness of the data, errors or omissions may occur due to limitations in the underlying data sources or data processing methods. If you believe a data point is inaccurate or have information that may improve the dataset, please contact the project team at socah.lab@yale.edu. In no event shall the authors, contributors, or copyright holders be liable for any claim, damages, or other liability, whether in an action of contract, tort, or otherwise, arising from, out of, or in connection with the data or the use or other dealings in the data. We welcome feedback and will review all reported discrepancies.”

title: Processing Pipeline
text:
Last Updated: September 1st, 2026


  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
    PHASE 1: CLEANING AND VALIDATING RAW DATA
      
        
          Step 1
          Manual standardisation of variable columns directly relevant to the analysis; the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) and Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) code columns. 
          
          The exported CSV is also converted to Parquet for more efficient data storage and loading.
        
        
          Step 2
          Clean and validate variable columns relevant to geocoding and spatial annotation.
          
          
            Optionally validate addresses against the USPS Addresses database and compress them to remove typographical errors.
            Use validated addresses to verify geocoordinates (longitude/latitude) via the U.S. Census Bureau Geocoder API.
            Use the resulting geocoordinates for spatial joining against U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line Shapefiles for census boundary annotation, including GEOIDs (block group, tract, county, state) and Core Statistical Areas (CBSA and CSA).
          
        
        
          Step 3
          Reshaping and annotation of the cleaned and validated data in preparation for metric calculation over unique American Business Identifier (ABI)/address combinations.
          
          
            Normalise SIC codes across unique ABI/address entries and translate them into religious affiliations (e.g., Hindu, Judaism, Christian).
            Fill in missing years-open values between filings shorter than the closure threshold.
            For ABIs filed under more than one address, annotate relocation metrics: number of moves; mean and maximum haversine distance (km) between addresses; and a Boolean flag indicating whether the move exceeded 5, 10, or 25 miles.
          
        
      
  
  
    PHASE 2
    Metric Generation
    
      
        Three metrics were requested for dashboard visualisation; all remaining metrics were intended to generate insights from the aggregation tables. All metrics are calculated across three stratifications: census boundary, religious affiliation, and decennial year (2000, 2010, and 2020).
        
        Metrics are first calculated at the block group level, the smallest census boundary, then aggregated upward to coarser boundaries, with values summed, averaged, or maxed at each step; this process is referred to as a rollup. Only GEOIDs are rolled up; ZCTA were not, as they do not crosswalk to census boundaries.
      
      
        
          Openings
          Total ABIs located in the unit/window, including those later excluded by a missingness flag.

          Closures & Reopenings
          Closure events (4+ inactive years following activity) and reopenings (2+ active years following a closure) are reported as counts per any event, per sq. mi., per 10k residents, average number of events, and max number of events.
          
          Each is reported for no_moves (excludes multi-address ABIs) and all (addresses for an ABI column-wise summed).

          Relocations
          Count of ABIs that moved, average moves per ABI, weighted-average and max move distance (km), and counts exceeding 5/10/25-mile thresholds.

          Missingness flags
          Address missing, address is a PO Box, or GEOID/ZCTA missing.
        
      
    
  
  
    USAGE NOTES
    Refer to Code/ for all scripts related to the pipeline. All files designed for the "2026 Formatted" dataset represent the most current version; any "2023 Formatted" scripts are retained for posterity, as they were used for the 2025 Summer prototype.
    
    Not all data used in this process can be or was shared. Users must consult their institution on how to gain access to the Data Axle business data processed here. All other ancillary data sources, such as the U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line Shapefiles, are listed with access instructions in the Data/Raw/ and Data/Results/ README.md files.
    
    The pipeline assumes the data is cleaned and validated anew and does not include a pathway for incorporating new yearly releases. While this functionality was not a priority in the current iteration, it can be incorporated in Phase 1, Step 2, reducing the time and financial costs associated with API validation.
